title: Human Cartilage Tissue Fabrication Using Three-dimensional Inkjet Printing Technology
protocol: Establish a bioprinting platform based on an HP Deskjet 500 thermal inkjet printer and HP 51626a black ink cartridge.
Remove the top plastic cover of the printer.
Detach the control panel from the cover.
Disconnect the three cable connections between the printer top portion and base.
Remove the printer top portion from the base.
On the printer top portion, remove small plastic and rubber accessories at the right-hand side under the ink cartridge.
Remove the base of the paper tray with springs.
Remove the metallic plate covering the plastic paper feeding bar.
Cut off the plastic paper feeding bar at the middle feeding wheel position using a hand saw or other cutting tool.
Remove the two paper feeding wheels exposed after the previous step.
Clean dust and debris using canned air and ethanol wipes.
Attach the printer top portion to the base.
UV sterilize the modified printer for at least 2 hours in a laminar flow hood before use.
Cut off the cap of an HP 51626a ink cartridge using a hand saw or other cutting tool.
Empty the ink from the cartridge.
Remove the filter that covers the bottom well reservoir of the cartridge.
Rinse the cartridge thoroughly with running tap water.
Ultrasonicate the cartridge in de-ionized (DI) water for 10 minutes to remove residual ink.
Examine the cartridge to make sure all the ink has been removed.
Rinse or spray the cartridge thoroughly with 70% ethanol for sterilization, followed by sterilized DI water.
Set up a long-wavelength ultraviolet lamp over the printing platform to provide simultaneous photopolymerization capacity.
Measure UV intensity at the printing platform using a UV light meter.
Adjust the distance between the UV lamp and the printer platform so the intensity at the printing subject is between 4-8 mW/cm2 (approximately 25 cm from lamp to the printer platform).
Dissolve PEGDA in PBS to a final concentration of 10% w/v.
Add photoinitiator I-2959 to a final concentration of 0.05% w/v.
Filter sterilize the solution.
Suspend cultured human chondrocytes in the prepared PEGDA solution at 5 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Turn on the printer and laptop.
Create a printing pattern of a solid circle with 4 mm in diameter using Microsoft Word or Adobe Photoshop.
Adjust the position of the pattern and make sure it will print exactly into the plastic mold.
Calculate the number of prints needed for scaffold thickness.
Load bioink into ink cartridge.
Cover ink cartridge with aluminum foil.
Send printing command to printer.
Pull paper sensor when printer starts printing.
Transfer printed neocartilage to a 24-well plate.
Add 1.5 ml culture medium to each well.
Incubate the printed neocartilage in LIVE/DEAD Viability/Cytotoxicity working solution at room temperature for 15 min in dark.
Cut cell-laden hydrogel in half.
Take fluorescent images of cutting area.
Count live (green) and dead (red) cells from five randomly taken images.
Calculate cell viability by dividing the number of live cells by total cells.
